Luis-apologies for the late note. Thank you for reporting the potential violating content from the FB page
of Fundación Contra el Terrorismo. As an update, we escalated this Page and the content provided and
while the Page as a whole doesn't violate our Standards, one of the posts that was flagged was confirmed
violating our Violence & Incitement policies and was removed.
Please let me know if you have any questions—happy to follow up.

Brian

Subject: Short fuse--FCT FB page inciting threats
This Message Is From an External Sender
Dear FB friends,
I know we have a pending meeting where we'll discuss protocols to address situations similar to these, but
wanted to bring the following to your attention:
USAID Administrator Samantha Power reached out yesterday to express concern regarding threats against
Guatemalan Judge Yassmin Barrios, a 2014 International Women of Courage awardee.
The Fundacion Contra el Terrorismo (FCT) targeted Judge Barrios most recently in a Nov. 1 and Nov 9 post
(see here). FCT is notorious for inciting threats and instigating spurious prosecutions against independent
justice operators (see here, for example). Three FCT reps were designated under Sec. 353 by the State
Department. Some time ago Twitter deplatformed their LordVader account but their Facebook continues
with such content.
In the Guatemalan context, the post regarding Barrios should be understood as a threat. In fact, in many
other instances, similar content contributed to judges and prosecutors going into exile. Could you look into
Thanks so much and looking forward to coming up with more streamlined procedures between AID and FB.

--
Luis Azurduy
Team Lead, Democracy, Human Rights and Governance
Office of Regional Sustainable Development
Bureau for Latin America and the Caribbean
United StatesAgency forInternational Development(USAID)
